standard_prerequisites.name: The affine-space intersection bound
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the dimension bound once the cones have been arranged to meet at the origin.

standard_prerequisites.name: Dimensions of fibres and of preimages under a smooth morphism
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the dimension of the fibres of the restrictions of V and W used to show they contain every fibre they meet.

core_obligations: Consider the morphism pi from punctured affine (n+1)-space onto projective n-space and note that it is surjective and smooth of relative dimension one with irreducible fibres (proof lines 6374-6392).
Deduce that the preimages of X and Y are nonempty closed subsets of dimension r+1 and s+1, and choose irreducible components V and W of those dimensions (proof lines 6393-6396).
Observe that V and W contain every fibre of pi they meet, using that the fibres of the restrictions to pi(V) and pi(W) have dimension at least one (proof lines 6397-6400).

Pass to the closures of V and W in affine (n+1)-space, note that the origin belongs to both because it lies in the closure of every fibre, and apply the affine-space intersection bound to conclude (proof lines 6401-6410).
proof_roadmap: Pull back to the affine cone over projective space.
Choose components of the cones of the right dimensions.
Use the fibre containment to force the origin into both closures.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that nonempty closed subsets X and Y of projective n-space with dim(X) + dim(Y) at least n meet, and that every component of the intersection has dimension at least r + s - n. The proof pulls the situation back along the surjective smooth morphism from punctured affine (n+1)-space to projective space, which has irreducible fibres of dimension one, so that the preimages have dimensions r+1 and s+1 (proof lines 6374-6393). It then chooses irreducible components V and W of the preimages of those dimensions, observes that they contain every fibre they meet, and passes to their closures in affine (n+1)-space, which contain the origin because the origin lies in the closure of every fibre; the affine intersection bound then gives the result (proof lines 6394-6410). H2: the cone construction and the fibre-containment observation are the substance.
